findings.title: Single-host concentration: host loss is total pipeline loss
findings.detail: All capture, storage, metrics, alerting and delivery run on one Ubuntu 24.04 KVM host with no warm standby; host loss is total monitoring loss (the edge buffers ~2 GiB, then blocks). Recorded owner-accepted from the 2026-10-05 run (documented RTO/RPO acceptance); no infra change. Fix path remains a warm standby or a tested RTO/RPO acceptance artifact.

findings.title: Vendored MCT tree remains tag-only under a blanket pin waiver; live stacks are now tag@digest and lock-covered
findings.detail: The live Wazuh/IRIS/OpenCanary stacks are now digest-pinned and lock-covered: automation/wazuh/multi-node/*.yml declare tag@sha256 refs (e.g. cloudflare/cloudflared:latest@sha256:e39ee8da..., nginx:stable@sha256:46ccc48f..., wazuh/*:4.14.7@sha256:...), pins/images.lock has 24 entries including them, the fast gate's compose-pin check passes, and live falcon_live_image_drift is 0. The residual is the vendored mct/compose tree (37 refs, 29 unpinned, 11 floating) under a blanket waiver root:mct/compose ref:* (review_by 2026-12-31) with P4 enforcement unimplemented; those services are staged, not running. Fix: scope the waiver per ref (as the Wazuh waivers do), implement P4 (import manifest + vendor-drift check), or make mct/compose non-deployable.

findings.title: Live ingest authentication is an HTTP basic-auth shared credential, not mTLS or request signing
findings.detail: edge->central ingest is authenticated by a shared credential over the internal network: config/vector/aggregator.yaml:25-28 and config/vector/edge.yaml:245-246 use auth strategy basic (falcon-vector-edge / ${VECTOR_INGEST_PW}). There is no per-device certificate identity and no replay/idempotency protection, so any holder of the shared credential can inject telemetry and a replay is not distinguishable. Fix: certificate/mTLS identity for ingest (the edge control plane already uses mTLS on 9443) or request signing + idempotency keys.
evidence: config/vector/aggregator.yaml:25-28 — auth: strategy: basic
config/vector/edge.yaml:245-246 — sink auth: strategy: basic

findings.title: Container-level memory and policy-restart alerting for central services is still absent
findings.detail: The ARCH-P1-003 failure mode (container OOM crash loop) was fixed by raising the aggregator limit to 1 GiB and adding drop visibility, but the container-level early-warning/restart signals remain unalerted: automation/validation/export_monitor_metrics.sh:697 exports falcon_container_mem_bytes, no rule references it (the live 86-rule set has only host-level memory rules 'Memory pressure', 'Host memory pressure (early warning)', 'Site host memory low'), and the only restart-loop rule is falcon-suricata-restart-loop (bootstrap/90-alerting.sh:418). A future container OOM would again surface only downstream (e2e failures / host pressure). Fix: add a rule on falcon_container_mem_bytes vs the declared limit (e.g. >85% for 15m) and a policy-restart-count rule for central services, with fixture proofs.
